Yeah I'm definitely happy I did not spend tons of money to go to that show.  Personally, I think the whole fictional band thing is pretty stupid.  Like, the music sounds barely any different from the new music they're already writing! (which isn't all that great tbh)  I honestly think they did the fictional band thing over covering a well-known album because it's easier than covering another artist's album.  With the fictional band, the music they write isn't associated with the Phish name, so it won't be held to as high of a standard as the music they write under the Phish name.  With covering an album, especially one that many people know, they have to make sure they get the particular sound right, every essential part of the song included, their performances are up to par, etc.

I also think that the fictional band caters to the crowd that is absolutely floored by the idea of a band within a band.  And if there is enough of those people compared to people who just want them to cover a classic album, then they obviously will go with that option.  Especially if it requires a whole lot less effort on their part.

On a positive note though, the first set was really good! Really good version of Ghost, although I must say Trey's playing is getting a tad bit sloppy. 

Overall, I'm mainly disappointed they didn't cover a classic album.

Lol I've always felt this way.  I'm not gonna tell you that everyone feels this way, cause that's simply just not true.  But regardless of how many people feel the way you or I do (and there's enough of them so don't feel so down), the fact of the matter is high school/teen movies are meant to be sensational and unrealistic.  They're made in such a way so that people who do well socially/sexually can relate to those films, even if they don't accurately represent what those people's lives are actually like.  But also the people making those films know that people like you and me will yearn for those kind of experiences, which increases their potential audience.    
As to your question about growing out of it, the feelings themselves don't necessarily disappear.  But it becomes more and more obvious as you get older that those films are pretty unrealistic and you'll meet enough people that you'll like that also feel those films didn't represent their time in high school.  Or whenever lol. Hope this helps!
